findings.claim: After a same-root claimant rebind—or registration of another claimant with the bearer—`ack` and `complete` accept the original claim token and mutate the handoff without requiring the active caller binding/identity/ctx to equal the tuple captured in `ct_claim`; old tokens are not fenced.
proof_refs: core.mjs:2346-2352 checks only claim existence/state and token hash; it never compares claimant.binding_id/identity/ctx with claim.claimant_binding_id/claimant_identity_digest/claimant_ctx_digest.
core.mjs:2362 constructs ACK claimant_authority_v1 from the current active claimant, allowing it to differ from the claim owner.
core.mjs:2583-2589 and core.mjs:2598 repeat the same omission for COMPLETE.

core.mjs:1264-1291 and core.mjs:1365-1386 preserve the stored claimant_authority_v1 during historical reconstruction without binding it back to the claim owner, so the cross-binding history remains accepted.
openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/specs/control-tower-identity-mode/spec.md:19 requires old generations/tokens after rebind to return CT_FENCE_MISMATCH.
openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/specs/control-tower-completion-attestation/spec.md:23 requires complete to match the claim tuple.

findings.claim: `validRollbackProof` accepts a contradictory rollback proof where a receipt has a valid but incorrect `read_back_digest`, asserts `read_back_matches_pre_state:true`, and copies the pre-start digest into `observed_boundary_digest`; no independent per-effect or aggregate read-back is actually verified.
proof_refs: core.mjs:1048-1052 validates only the read-back digest's syntax and never compares it with effect.pre_state_digest.
core.mjs:1061-1064 trusts the receipt booleans and caller-supplied observed boundary equality instead of recomputing either from read-back digests.
openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/design.md:1315 requires independent read-back equality for every effect and the aggregate boundary.
openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/specs/control-tower-completion-attestation/spec.md:43 and :55-58 require independent read-back proof before rollback succeeds.
test/lifecycle.test.mjs:758-763 tests malformed digest syntax but not a well-formed digest contradicting `read_back_matches_pre_state:true`.

findings.claim: The capability-advertised P5 MCP schemas do not encode the normative nested shapes or limits: any object is advertised as a valid `effect_manifest` or `committed_result`, including objects with missing or extra members.
proof_refs: openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/design.md:1398 requires schemas encoding exact required fields, enums, limits, and explicit-null rejection.
Core validation still rejects malformed values, so this is an advertised MCP-contract defect rather than an authority bypass.

findings.claim: A forbidden non-canonical `-0` effect index is accepted as index 0 and canonicalized into persisted evidence rather than rejected; P5 generation fields likewise accept `-0` through `safeEpoch`.
proof_refs: In JavaScript `-0 !== 0` is false, so core.mjs:1016 accepts `effect_index:-0` for the first effect.
core.mjs:786 accepts `-0` because Number.isSafeInteger(-0) and `-0 >= 0` are both true.
The local JCS helper serializes `-0` through JSON.stringify as `0`, allowing the forbidden input to be normalized and persisted.
openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/design.md:1297 explicitly requires effect manifests to reject `-0`.
